tips: Clear and reset
clear hides the visible output; reset reinitializes a garbled terminal. Neither guarantees history is erased.
Command history
Use history or Ctrl+R in Bash to recall past commands. Avoid putting passwords in commands.
Frozen application
Identify the correct PID with ps or top. Ctrl+C interrupts a foreground terminal command; kill can signal a selected process.
Tab completion
Press Tab to complete a command or path; behavior varies by shell.
Temporary aliases
alias ll='ls -lah' creates a shortcut for the current shell session.
Permanent aliases
Put a reviewed alias in the correct shell startup file, such as ~/.bashrc; syntax varies by shell.
Chain commands
A ; B runs B after A. A && B runs B on success. A || B runs B on failure.
Command syntax
Check man, --help or tldr; optional fields in synopsis are usually not literal brackets.
Cursor navigation
Ctrl+A goes to beginning and Ctrl+E to end in common Bash editing mode.
Redirection
> overwrites or creates a file; >> appends; < supplies input; 2> redirects error output.
Special characters
* and ? match filenames, quotes group text, backslash escapes characters, # starts comments in ordinary shell contexts.
View permissions
ls -l displays file type and owner, group and other permission triplets.
Modify permissions
chmod changes access rights; prefer minimum necessary privileges.
Octal permissions
4 = read, 2 = write, 1 = execute. 600 grants owner read/write only.
Background jobs
A trailing & starts a job in the background; jobs lists shell jobs and fg brings a job forward.
Schedule tasks
cron is a scheduling service where supported; Android and container setups may not provide it.
